questions.q: What problem do both package configurations and the parameters/environments pattern exist to solve?
options: How a package picks up the right environment-specific values (connection strings, file paths) automatically, without hand-editing the package for dev, test, and production
How to speed up data flow buffer throughput
How to add new system variables to a package
How to encrypt sensitive columns inside a data flow
questions.explain: Every configuration mechanism in this lesson answers the same question: where does the right value for this environment come from, and how does the package pick it up without manual edits at each promotion?

questions.q: Under the Package Deployment Model, what does Microsoft recommend using instead of parameters?
options: Package configurations — parameters aren't invoked under this deployment model and can cause the package to fail
Environment variables set in Windows only
Hardcoded values, since the Package Deployment Model doesn't support any dynamic configuration
SSISDB environment references
questions.explain: Microsoft's own guidance is that if you're deploying with the Package Deployment Model, use configurations — a package with project parameters deployed this way isn't guaranteed to execute correctly, since parameters aren't called during that model's execution.

questions.q: What are the three types of package configurations mentioned for the legacy model?
options: XML configuration file, SQL Server table, and (Windows) environment variable
JSON file, CSV file, and registry key
Project parameter, package parameter, and SSISDB environment variable
Design value, server value, and execution value
questions.explain: Legacy package configurations can be stored in an XML file, a SQL Server table, or read from a Windows environment variable.

questions.q: In the Project Deployment Model, what server-side object actually decides which set of values a deployed project's parameters resolve to?
options: The environment reference linking the project to one specific SSISDB environment
The package's own Parameters tab
A Windows environment variable on the SSIS server
The Execute Package dialog box, every single time the package runs
questions.explain: The environment reference is what links a deployed project to one specific SSISDB environment (like DEV or PROD); repointing that reference changes which environment's variable values the project's parameters resolve to, with no redeployment needed.

questions.q: What does the Integration Services Project Conversion Wizard do?
options: Migrates a configuration-based package to the Project Deployment Model, generating equivalent parameters from its existing configurations
Converts a Flat File connection manager into an OLE DB connection manager
Automatically writes property expressions for every task in a package
Deletes unused system variables from a package
questions.explain: The Conversion Wizard is Microsoft's tooling for moving a legacy, configuration-based package onto the Project Deployment Model, generating parameters equivalent to its existing configurations.
